masthead.name: The Analyst Collective
masthead.tagline: Daily research for investment banking and industrials
masthead.notice: DEMONSTRATION CONTENT. The stories below are illustrative placeholders written to test the layout. They are not verified news. Live, sourced reporting will replace them in a later stage.

articles.headline: [Demo] Defence maker reports order inflow rise; execution timelines to watch
articles.deck: Illustrative story showing how an order-book update is presented.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional listed defence company disclosed new contract awards in its exchange filing. The example is used to demonstrate layout only.
keyFacts: Contract value: not disclosed in this demo
Status: contract awarded, revenue not yet recognised
articles.whyItMatters: Order inflows give revenue visibility, but revenue is recognised only as execution progresses. Analysts separate awarded contracts from letters of intent and memoranda of understanding.
articles.ibAngle: A strong order book can support equity fundraising or a private placement. Bankers would examine margins and cash conversion before pricing.
articles.sectorImplications: Suppliers of components and sub-assemblies may see higher volumes. Competitors bidding for similar tenders may face tougher pricing.

articles.headline: [Demo] Mid-cap auto components firm explores sale of non-core unit
articles.deck: Illustrative divestiture story for the Investment Banking & Deals section.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional company is described as exploring a sale of a non-core business. No transaction has been announced in this demo.
articles.whyItMatters: Non-core divestments can simplify a balance sheet and unlock value, but they often take months to reach signing.
articles.ibAngle: Would typically involve a sell-side process, buyer list, and valuation using comparable multiples. Do not assume an adviser unless a reliable source confirms it.
articles.sectorImplications: Potential buyers include private equity funds and strategic competitors. The sale could reshape supplier relationships.

articles.headline: [Demo] Battery cell maker announces proposed plant; construction not yet started
articles.deck: Illustrative example of distinguishing a proposed investment from a completed project.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional battery company announced a plan for a new cell plant. The plan remains subject to approvals and funding.
keyFacts: Capacity: not disclosed in this demo
articles.whyItMatters: Battery capacity is central to EV unit economics. Announced capacity often differs from capacity actually built and running.
articles.ibAngle: Large capex plans may require project finance, a rights issue, or incentive-linked funding. Watch for the funding structure.
articles.sectorImplications: Carmakers and cell suppliers may secure supply, while critical mineral demand could rise.

articles.headline: [Demo] Regulator issues consultation paper on disclosure norms
articles.deck: Illustrative regulatory item showing the five-point analysis format.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional consultation paper proposes changes to disclosure requirements for listed companies. Comments are invited before any change takes effect.
articles.whyItMatters: Consultation papers signal direction. Final rules may differ in timing and scope.
articles.ibAngle: Disclosure changes affect deal timelines, prospectus content, and due diligence scope.
articles.sectorImplications: Companies planning fundraising or listings should track the consultation outcome.

articles.headline: [Demo] Central bank holds rates; markets weigh inflation outlook
articles.deck: Illustrative macro story for Markets & Economy.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional central bank kept its policy rate unchanged and signalled data dependence.
articles.whyItMatters: Rate expectations affect valuations, borrowing costs, and the timing of IPOs and bond issues.
articles.ibAngle: Issuers often accelerate or delay capital markets activity depending on rate direction.
articles.sectorImplications: Rate-sensitive sectors such as capital goods and real estate react most.

articles.headline: [Demo] New tariffs on industrial inputs prompt supply-chain review
articles.deck: Illustrative trade story for Global Affairs.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional government announced tariffs on certain industrial inputs, effective from a future date.
articles.whyItMatters: Input tariffs raise costs for manufacturers that rely on imports, and can shift sourcing decisions.
articles.ibAngle: Companies may need to reassess margins in valuation models and in any pending deal.
articles.sectorImplications: Domestic producers may benefit, while importers face margin pressure.

articles.headline: [Demo] Industrial automation firm launches AI-based maintenance platform
articles.deck: Illustrative product story for Technology & AI.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional automation company launched a software platform for predictive maintenance of factory equipment.
articles.whyItMatters: Recurring software revenue can improve margin quality compared with one-time equipment sales.
articles.ibAngle: Software-led industrial businesses often attract private equity interest and command higher multiples.
articles.sectorImplications: Other machinery makers may need similar offerings to keep pace.

articles.headline: [Demo] Reading an order book: what to check beyond the headline number
articles.deck: A sample analyst note explaining how to interpret order-book disclosures.
articles.whatHappened: This sample note explains how to read an order book, including execution timelines, client concentration, and margin profile.
articles.whyItMatters: A large headline order book can hide slow execution or thin margins.
articles.ibAngle: Order-book quality affects how bankers present growth stories in offering documents.
articles.sectorImplications: Peers can be compared on order-book cover, which is order book divided by annual revenue.

articles.headline: [Demo] Carmaker reports quarterly volume growth; margins under pressure
articles.deck: Illustrative automobile story showing volume and margin tracking.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional carmaker reported higher domestic volumes and lower EBITDA margin for the quarter.
keyFacts: Volume growth: shown as demo figure
EBITDA margin: lower year on year (demo)
articles.whyItMatters: Volume growth without margin expansion suggests discounting or higher input costs.
articles.ibAngle: Margin trends shape valuation multiples used in IPO pricing and merger analysis.
articles.sectorImplications: Suppliers face the same input cost trend, and dealers see inventory effects.

articles.headline: [Demo] Two-wheeler maker completes stake purchase in EV joint venture
articles.deck: Illustrative joint venture story for the deals section.
articles.whatHappened: A fictional two-wheeler maker completed the purchase of a stake in an EV venture.
articles.whyItMatters: Joint ventures let incumbents learn EV technology without full balance-sheet exposure.
articles.ibAngle: Such deals are often structured with staged funding and put and call options.
articles.sectorImplications: Other incumbents may seek similar partnerships.

articles.headline: [Demo] Government announces incentive scheme for domestic component makers
articles.whatHappened: A fictional ministry announced an incentive scheme for domestic manufacturing of components. Detailed guidelines are pending.
articles.whyItMatters: Incentives are often linked to sales or investment thresholds, which determine who benefits.
articles.ibAngle: Incentive-backed capacity can improve the investment case for capex-heavy listed companies.
articles.sectorImplications: Global component suppliers may localise production to qualify.
